issues.title: [Foundation] Qualify and pin the Jujutsu development baseline
issues.body:
## Initiative
Foundation and Falsification

## Objective
Replace the reported local `jj 0.23.0` development assumption with a supported, pinned Jujutsu baseline whose required behavior is demonstrated by executable fixtures.

## Effect class
external_read

## Research basis
Gordian depends on exact commit/change identity separation, workspaces, sibling/parent/multi-parent topology, first-class conflicts, operation recovery, tags, and revision-scoped verification. Current Jujutsu research targets a release new enough for `jj run`, which was introduced well after 0.23.

Knowledge-graph nodes: `tool:jujutsu`, `source:jj-docs`, `experiment:jj-baseline`.

## Dependencies
None

## Dependency rationale
This Atom is a causal root of the implementation Mission: every other Atom that relies on source-plane behaviour depends on this qualification, and it depends on nothing itself.

## Acceptance
- Document the minimum supported Jujutsu release and why.
- Upgrade/bootstrap the Codex development environment reproducibly.
- Add contract fixtures for change-ID persistence across rewrites, exact commit IDs, isolated workspaces, sibling changes, causal ancestry, multi-parent integration, conflict representation/resolution, operation history/recovery, and tags.
- Confirm `jj run` is available on the pinned release and record its presence; contract tests for `jj run` semantics are owned by #33.
- Make unsupported behavior an explicit adapter constraint rather than an assumption.
- Record the exact Jujutsu binary/version (`jj --version` output) in the contract-fixture manifest produced by this Atom's Verification fixtures and committed to the repository.

## Verification
Executable CLI contract tests against a disposable fixture repository.

## Benchmark obligation
Owned elsewhere: workspace spawn is #30, revision materialization and verification are #33, integration is #32, and status/query latency is #29. This Atom carries no benchmark obligation of its own.

## Objective

- Admission takes an `IntegrationCandidate` built over the current frontier and a batch; it never admits a bare Candidate.
- The admission witness is the ten conjuncts of `docs/spec/mission-graph.md` `## Accepted frontier`, including `parents_unadmitted`, `lease_valid_at_freeze`, and `evidence_provenance_valid`; admission rejects candidates failing any of them.

- The required verifier manifest is complete and every required result passes and freshly matches the exact candidate.
- The frontier CAS is an expected-version append of `CandidateAdmitted` to the canonical event log, followed by an idempotent bookmark move and a `FrontierMoved` append; crash recovery re-drives unmatched intents and closes an unrecoverable intent with `AdmissionAborted`.
- The witness is evaluated at a named `ProjectionVersion` and committed under a `WitnessGuard` on that version as well as on `FrontierVersion`; `CandidateAdmitted` records the witness itself, not only its digest.
- Admission requires a live exclusive lease on `LeaseSubject::Coordinator(project)`; completion is a single conditional transactional append of `FrontierMoved` plus every `AtomSatisfied`.
- A candidate whose `admission_attempts` (counting `AdmissionPreempted` **and** `IntegrationConflictObserved`) reaches `MAX_ADMISSION_ATTEMPTS` (3) is admitted in an exclusive single-member batch, in FIFO order; after `MAX_EXCLUSIVE_ATTEMPTS` it is closed with `AdmissionRejected`.
- Every false witness conjunct appends `AdmissionRejected { subject, conjunct, detail }`, releases the batch claims, and returns the Atom to a defined state; admission never fails silently.
- Define `Acceptable` in `formal/Gordian/Acceptance.lean` in terms of `Conflict.DeclaredNonInterfering`, `Evidence.Compatible` and the `Authority` predicates rather than opaque `Prop` fields.

Determine whether Gordian's Lean models, independent proof checking, and Lean/Rust conformance harness catch meaningful substrate defects beyond Rust types, property/model tests, mutation tests, and review at a justified engineering cost.

## Effect class

## Research basis

## Dependencies

## Dependency rationale

## Experimental design
Seed or mine defects in graph acyclicity, Quark boundary policy, dispatch prerequisites, evidence mismatch, authority, candidate admission, replay, lease transitions, and compare-and-swap behavior. Evaluate verification stacks incrementally rather than crediting all tools jointly.

## Conditions
A. compiler/types + unit/integration tests
B. A + generated property/state-machine tests
C. B + mutation/fuzz/concurrency methods appropriate to the defect
D. C + Lean model/proof obligations
E. D + Lean/Rust differential conformance testing

## Measurements
- defect classes found uniquely/earlier by each layer
- false confidence or model/implementation mismatch
- proof/specification authoring and maintenance time
- CI/runtime/dependency cost
- regression prevention after refactors
- theorem triviality versus engineering relevance
- assumptions that dominate the result

## Pre-registration
Class: **classification** (`docs/testing/statistical-contract.md` section 2), the class `experiments/formal-value/README.md` already names for this study. The five verification stacks are the predictors and the seeded-defect corpus is the single labeled corpus they are all scored on. Registered before any data is inspected; the analysis runs once, after all runs complete. An amendment requires a new PlanRevision with its own rationale and is never made mid-experiment. Every slot below is taken from the `classification` column of the section 2 table and none of them is overridden here.

H0: Condition E (Lean model plus Lean/Rust differential conformance) does not lower expected total cost against condition C (property, mutation, fuzz and concurrency methods).
Primary metric: expected total cost - missed-defect cost plus formalization authoring and maintenance cost, per seeded defect, normalized to the baseline stack's cost, unit: normalized verification-cost units, read from `ExperimentRun.metrics["expected_total_cost"]` in the #75 ledger, reported with a stratified bootstrap 95% CI over 10000 resamples whose half-width on the primary is at most 0.05.
Minimum effect size: delta versus the baseline predictor C of at least 0.10 normalized cost units, a 10% relative cost reduction; below that, the marginal Lean obligation is removed for the affected semantics.
Secondary metrics, reported under Holm-Bonferroni over the four predictor-versus-baseline comparisons (A, B, D and E each against C): unique seeded-defect detection rate (`unique_detection_rate_over_C`), detection latency, proof authoring and maintenance hours, and CI wall-clock. No conclusion is stated on a secondary metric alone.
Corpus: one frozen labeled corpus of at least 200 seeded defects, 40 in each of the five defect classes, every defect scored under all five condition stacks A-E, carrying at least 50 positives, where a positive is a seeded defect the baseline stack C fails to detect. A corpus with fewer than 50 positives is re-seeded and re-frozen before any predictor is scored.
Baseline condition: C - property/state-machine tests plus mutation, fuzz and concurrency methods appropriate to the defect.
Stopping rule: fixed corpus, frozen before any predictor is scored; no interim analysis, and no seed is added after scoring begins.
Exclusion rule: a seeded defect is excluded only when it fails to compile under one or more conditions (`fault_class = seed_invalid`), applied by `scripts/apply-exclusions.py`, and is replaced by a re-seeded defect of the same class before the corpus is frozen; every excluded seed is retained with its reason.

Condition E is retained for a class of semantics only when its expected total cost on that class's stratum is at least 0.10 normalized cost units below condition C's, with the stratified bootstrap 95% CI on the delta excluding zero. The current graph is useful for traversal but still models most nodes as `id + type + name + summary + relations`. issues.title: [Foundation] Implement reproducible run ledger and statistical analysis contract
issues.body:
## Initiative
Foundation and Falsification

## Objective
Make Gordian experiments reproducible and resistant to cherry-picking, noisy microbenchmarks, hidden exclusions, and post-hoc metric selection while keeping scientific interpretation separate from the Rust runtime.

## Effect class
idempotent_write

## Research basis
Knowledge-graph nodes: `experiment:foundation-benchmarks`, `foundation:benchmarking`, `artifact:research-methodology`.

## Dependencies
- #3
- #5
- #71

## Dependency rationale
#3 supplies the seeded workloads, #5 the benchmark harness, and #71 the typed research record schema the ledger's records are instances of. The thin Python runner that executes trial matrices is #37, which depends on this Atom rather than the other way round (D3).

## Acceptance
- Define a machine-readable ExperimentProtocol and ExperimentRun manifest with hypothesis, falsification condition, conditions, controls, workload/seed, source/toolchain/environment identities, budget, metrics, **minimum effect size**, **baseline condition**, analysis plan, stopping rule, exclusions, raw artifacts, and outcome.
- `ExperimentProtocol.analysis_plan` requires `primary_metric`, `effect_size`, `min_n`, `multiplicity`, and `stopping_rule` as non-optional fields, with a `#[test]` per field asserting that a manifest missing it fails to deserialize.
- `ExperimentProtocol.class` is required and must be one of the four classes of `docs/testing/statistical-contract.md`; a protocol with no class is invalid.
- Rust validates manifests, identities, required fields, artifact digests, and metric schemas.
- Thin Python executes trial matrices and statistical analysis without redefining scheduler/evidence/domain semantics.
- Preserve every attempted run, failure, timeout, exclusion, and reason; do not retain only successful trials.
- Report effect sizes and uncertainty when supported by the design; report missing statistical power/assumptions rather than inventing confidence.
- The analysis plan (paired vs unpaired, seed treatment, and pseudoreplication guard) is a required field of the ExperimentProtocol, fixed before the first confirmatory run. Rust rejects (a) a protocol missing that field and (b) an ExperimentRun whose analysis plan differs from the protocol it cites.
- Separate exploratory results from confirmatory/decision-bearing runs.
- Link results to Hypothesis, Decision, Algorithm, Benchmark, issue, code commit, and knowledge graph nodes.

## Pre-registration label binding
Every experiment issue's `## Pre-registration` block uses six labels. A validator script checks each block against this table and fails on any unmapped or missing label.

| Issue label | ExperimentProtocol field |
| --- | --- |
| `H0:` | `hypothesis.null` |
| `Primary metric:` | `analysis_plan.primary_metric` |
| `Minimum effect size:` | `analysis_plan.effect_size.minimum_relevant` |
| `Seeds/trials:` | `analysis_plan.min_n` and `workload.seeds` |
| `Baseline condition:` | `conditions[].baseline` (exactly one true) |
| `Exclusion rule:` | `exclusions.rule` |

## Verification
Schema/property tests including one named fixture test per required `analysis_plan` field (`missing_primary_metric`, `missing_effect_size`, `missing_min_n`, `missing_multiplicity`, `missing_stopping_rule`, `analysis_plan_mismatch`), malformed/missing-artifact fixtures, deterministic synthetic analysis cases, deliberate cherry-pick/exclusion violations, and rerun-from-manifest tests.

## Benchmark obligation

issues.title: [Jujutsu Change Plane] Implement Git worktree source adapter behind the source-adapter trait
issues.body:
## Initiative
Jujutsu Change Plane

## Objective
Implement a second source plane behind the `SourceAdapter` trait defined by #29, using Git worktrees, so
that #34 can compare two substrates through one trait with nothing else varying. This Atom exists because
#34's comparison is otherwise a comparison against a substrate no Atom builds (D4, G-412).

## Effect class
idempotent_write

## Research basis
Knowledge-graph nodes: `tool:git`, `experiment:jj-vs-git`, `artifact:jj-adapter`.

## Dependencies
- #29
- #30
- #31
- #32
- #33

## Acceptance
- Implement `SourceAdapter` for Git worktrees in `crates/gordian-source/src/git/`, realizing every
  operation of `docs/protocols/source-adapter-contract.md` section 2.
- `snapshot(base)` creates an **exact-base worktree**: the worktree contains exactly `base` and no ambient
  working-copy state, and each call returns a distinct `WorkspaceId`.
- Git has no native evolving-change identity, so the adapter **synthesizes** `logical_change_id`,
  persists the `logical_change_id -> exact_state_id` mapping durably under `.git/gordian/changes/`, and
  records the synthesis as an adapter-scoped provenance fact. The mapping survives `git gc`, worktree
  removal, and process restart, and the document naming its storage location is
  `docs/protocols/source-adapter-contract.md` section 1.
- `exact_state_id` is the Git commit id and is unique per exact tree/parent state; two different states
  never share one.
- `freeze(change)` implements **candidate freeze**: it returns the `exact_state_id` of the change's current
  content, returns the same id when called twice with no intervening mutation, and a different id after any
  mutation. A frozen state is retained by a Gordian-owned ref so it is never garbage-collected while a
  Candidate references it.
- `integrate(parents)` supports **multi-parent** integration (octopus or iterated two-parent merge, with the
  ordering rule documented) and returns `Conflict` with regions rather than a partially merged state.
- `conflicts(state)` is total on any state the adapter produced. Git cannot persist an unresolved
  **conflict** in a commit, so the adapter materializes conflicted merges into a Gordian-owned conflict
  record rather than leaving them only in an index.
- `verify(state, manifest)` executes against a **read-only** materialization at a **detached** HEAD and
  never mutates the candidate state or the ambient working copy.
- Recovery reads the Git **reflog** plus the durable change mapping to reconstruct workspace, change, and
  candidate provenance after a crash, since Git has no operation log equivalent to `jj op log`.
- Every capability the backend cannot supply natively is surfaced as an explicit **capability flag** on the
  adapter (for example `native_logical_change_id: false`, `native_conflict_representation: false`), and
  Gordian domain code branches on the flag, never on the adapter name.
- The adapter is selected by a single configuration value drawn from the closed set `{jj, git}`; nothing
  above `gordian-source` reads it.
- The shared adapter-contract suite `crates/gordian-source/tests/adapter_contract.rs` runs unchanged
  against this adapter with **no skipped tests**: a capability this backend lacks is expressed as a
  documented synthesized behaviour, not as an ignored test.
- Command invocation is structured with explicit **argv/cwd/env** and bounded parsing of porcelain
  machine-readable output; no shell-string interpolation is used for repository operations.
- The adapter identifies the **git binary/version**, rejects unsupported baselines explicitly, and records
  the version in every evidence record it produces.
- `AdapterError` variants are classified `transient` or `permanent` exactly as the Jujutsu adapter
  classifies its own.

## Non-goals
- Making Git the default source plane. The default is decided by #34, not by this Atom.
- Reimplementing Jujutsu semantics on Git. Where the backends genuinely differ, the difference is a
  documented capability flag and a documented synthesis, not a simulation.

## Verification
The shared adapter-contract suite `crates/gordian-source/tests/adapter_contract.rs`, run against both
adapters with no skipped tests, plus Git-specific fixtures for worktree isolation, synthesized
`logical_change_id` persistence across `git gc` and worktree removal, detached-HEAD verification,
multi-parent integration, conflict materialization, and reflog-based recovery.

## Benchmark obligation
Measure workspace spawn, freeze, integrate, conflict enumeration, verify-at-revision, and frontier move
latency on the same #3 workloads as the Jujutsu adapter, recording every run through the #75 experiment run
ledger so #34's comparison reads measured values rather than impressions.

issues.milestone: Agent Execution and Thin Python Orchestration
issues.body:
## Initiative
Agent Execution and Thin Python Orchestration

## Objective
Extend #37's foundation subset with worker-process and agent-harness launching: the part of Python
orchestration that starts, supervises, and records real workers rather than deterministic subprocesses.
This is the worker-launch extension split out of #37 by D1 so that the foundation subset is not blocked on
the worker protocol (#35) and the worker adapter (#36).

## Effect class
compensatable_write

## Research basis
Knowledge-graph nodes: `artifact:python-orchestration`, `artifact:agent-contract`, `experiment:isolation-coordination-ablation`.

## Dependencies
- #2
- #5
- #35
- #36
- #37

## Acceptance
- Launch worker processes and coding-agent harnesses through #35's worker protocol and #36's Rust worker
  adapter, reusing #37's subprocess runner rather than re-implementing it.
- A worker receives only its assigned workspace, capabilities, and budget; the launcher cannot widen either.
- Record model and provider configuration for every launched agent worker - provider, model id, sampling
  parameters, and prompt/tool configuration digest - as part of the run record, so a trial is reproducible
  from its manifest.
- Supervise the worker: timeout, cancellation, abandonment, and resource observation are normalized into
  ExecutionAttempt events through #36 rather than being interpreted in Python.
- Model and tool calls are recorded as nondeterministic effects; a replay never silently re-invokes the
  model.
- Python contains no independent implementation of readiness, scheduling safety, evidence freshness,
  admission, lease, capability, or Mission satisfaction semantics; the launcher decides nothing the Rust
  substrate decides.
- Ruff and the orchestration test suite pass independently.

## Non-goals
- Owning the seed matrix, subprocess primitives, or raw artifact capture. Those are #37 and are consumed
  here unchanged.
- Owning the worker protocol or sandbox envelope. Those are #35 and #36.

## Verification
Deterministic fixture-worker launches, provider-configuration recording fixtures, timeout and cancellation
races, capability-denial cases, and an integration test asserting that a launched agent worker's run record
reproduces its manifest byte for byte.

## Benchmark obligation
Measure launcher overhead separately from model latency, so worker-spawn cost is attributable to the
orchestration layer rather than absorbed into provider round-trip time.
